one_liner: A senior Marine Corps contracting officer-track role at Quantico planning, negotiating, and administering complex FAR, CSO, and OTA contracts for major programs.
fit_summary: This NH-3 role requires a year of GS-11-equivalent specialized experience in FAR-based contracting, Commercial Solution Openings, Other Transaction Authority, and cost and pricing evaluation. Nothing on file shows Daniel has done hands-on contracting or pricing work. Daniel's IEM consulting background and relationship skills only help if that job involved real procurement, proposal pricing, or contract administration duties.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public), so Daniel can apply as a U.S. citizen without federal status.

At least one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-11/NH-02 in FAR contracting (commercial and noncommercial), CSO, and OTA procedures; long-term pre-/post-award actions; and cost and pricing evaluation.
Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance required, which means a lengthy background investigation and eligibility for SCI access.
This is a public notice flyer, not an application portal; you must follow the separate 'How to Apply' directions to be considered.
Resume is limited to 2 pages; DoD 1102 roles typically also carry acquisition certification and education requirements, so confirm these in the full announcement.
strategy: Assess honestly whether your IEM role touched procurement, such as proposal pricing, cost volumes, task order management, subcontracts, or contractor-side compliance with FAR clauses. If it did not, treat this as a target for later and apply to GS-1102 trainee or Acquisition Development Program roles (GS-5/7/9) instead.

If you did support government contracts at IEM, frame the work from the contractor side. Describe the task orders, period-of-performance milestones, deliverables, and modifications you handled, using the posting's terms (post-award, contractor performance, cost).
State hours per week and month/year dates for each job so HR can verify one full year at the GS-11 equivalent level. Keep everything within 2 pages.
Find and follow the 'How to Apply' instructions linked from the flyer before the November 27, 2026 close date, since applications are not accepted through the flyer itself.
Be ready for SCI investigation paperwork (SF-86). List any foreign contacts, finances, and residence history accurately from the start.
resume_bullets: Supported [number] government emergency-management task orders valued at [$ amount] for [client agency], tracking deliverables, milestones, and [modifications/funding issues] through post-award performance.
Prepared [cost volumes/pricing inputs/labor estimates] for [number] proposals responding to [agency] solicitations, coordinating with [team] to meet submission deadlines.
Coordinated with [client contracting officer representatives/program staff] in [number] working groups to resolve [delivery/scope] issues and recommend corrective actions.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would choose between a FAR-based contract, a Commercial Solution Opening, and an Other Transaction agreement for a prototype requirement.
Describe a time you evaluated cost or pricing data and what you concluded.
How have you handled a contractor missing a critical milestone?
How do you keep complex approvals on schedule when multiple stakeholders are involved?
watch_outs: The qualification bar is high: without documented FAR/OTA contracting and pricing experience, you will likely be rated not qualified.
The SCI clearance requirement can delay your start date for months.
This is an anticipated-vacancy flyer; positions may never be filled, and no Notice of Result letters will be sent.
The posting lists no promotion potential, so NH-3 is the ceiling for this role.
